land.text: the old Shang heartland round Zhaoge: after the Duke of Zhou defeated the rebellion, 'Kang Shu, a younger brother of King Wu of Zhou was given a fief centred on Zhaoge'

predecessors.note: Enfeoffed by the Zhou after the Rebellion of the Three Guards; the page gives no boundary.

land.text: Yewang, where Wey's ruler was relocated in 241 and where the state survived 'nominally as a Qin vassal with no real independence'; Qin Er Shi deposed Lord Jiao in 209

successors.note: Puyang went to Qin in 241 (the ledger); the traditional end is 209, but a modern revision (Hirase Takao, Zhou Zhenhe) ends Lord Jiao's reign in 221.

capitals.name: Zhaoge (Qi County, Hebi)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Zhaoge: c. 1040-661 BCE'; the Rong attacked Zhaoge in 660, killing Duke Yi. The modern site is the researcher's placing.

capitals.name: Chuqiu
capitals.note: Infobox 'Chuqiu: 659-629 BCE'; moved there after the restoration with Duke Huan of Qi's help. Coordinates (Hua County area) are the researcher's placing; the page gives no modern site.

capitals.name: Diqiu (Puyang)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Diqiu: 629-241 BCE'. Equating Diqiu with Puyang is the researcher's reading: the page says only that by 320 Wey 'controlled only the county of Puyang' and that Qin captured Puyang in 241.

capitals.name: Yewang
capitals.note: Infobox 'Yewang: 241-209 BCE'; the coordinates (Qinyang, Henan) are the researcher's placing.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape carried back to the fief centred on Zhaoge

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's first Wey shape: the fief of Kang Shu centred on Zhaoge, c. 1040. Cliopatria's 750 shape carried back; Zhaoge (the Qi County, Hebi, site) lies on the western edge of its bounding box (114.2E). The page gives no area or boundary.

7,027 km2 for -750..-551, the Zhaoge-Chuqiu-Diqiu plain north of the Yellow River. The infobox gives no area; the three capitals (Zhaoge to 661, Chuqiu 659-629, Diqiu from 629) all fall inside or on the edge of the shape. Unverified for size: the page gives no boundary. Xing's land (Yiyi, Liaocheng) taken in 635 is not in the shape (ledger).
6,909 km2 for -550..-451: one cell passes to Jin at 550. Page silent; no Wey border is dated between 629 and 346 on the pages opened. Unverified: page budget.

5,875 km2 for -450..-405: Cliopatria passes 9 cells to Jin at 450 (jin.json records the matching gain, also page-silent). The page says Wey 'became attached to the House of Zhao of Jin' after the Kuaikui-Duke Chu conflict (undated). Unverified.
5,800 km2 for -404..-367: one cell to Wei. Page silent; the Wei page opened has nothing on Wey. Unverified.
5,684 km2 for -366..-351: 2 cells to Zhao. The page gives no loss; 'downgraded to marquis in 346' is a title, not land. Unverified.

correction.text: the shape unchanged for -350..-321; from -320 the Puyang shape of wey_-320

keyframe_review.note: 5,700 km2 for -350..-285, but the page says that 'by 320 BCE' Wey 'controlled only the county of Puyang', roughly a quarter of this shape. Correction: the shape holds to -321, then wey_-320 (Puyang) replaces it. The infobox has no area; the text is the check.

correction.text: the county of Puyang, all that Wey controlled by 320

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -320..-242: 'by 320 BCE Wey controlled only the county of Puyang', which Qin captured in 241. A 25 km radius round Puyang stands for the county (the gazetteer has no county units); the page gives no boundary.

correction.text: superseded by wey_-320: only Puyang remained

keyframe_review.note: 5,803 km2 for -284..-257 in Cliopatria; in these years the page has Wey a dependency of Wei ('In 252 BCE, Wei installed its son-in-law as ruler, making Wey a dependency of Wei') and Lord Huai killed by King Anxi of Wei in 254. Superseded by wey_-320: only Puyang remained.

correction.text: superseded by wey_-320: only Puyang remained

keyframe_review.note: 5,803 km2 for -256..-248, the last Cliopatria shape; Wey continued to 209. Superseded by wey_-320 up to -242, then wey_-241 (Yewang).

correction.text: Yewang, the last seat of the Wey ruler, a nominal Qin vassal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -241..-209, years Cliopatria lacks: Qin captured Puyang 'during its attack on Wei' and Wey's ruler was relocated to Yewang, where the state survived 'nominally as a Qin vassal with no real independence'. The 20 km circle at Yewang (Qinyang, Henan) is the researcher's placing of a seat the page names without a place.

ledger.note: c. 1040: the Zhou enfeoff Kang Shu at Zhaoge and Wey begins on the old Shang heartland north of the Yellow River. 'Kang Shu, a younger brother of King Wu of Zhou was given a fief centred on Zhaoge' after the Duke of Zhou defeated the rebellion; infobox 'Zhaoge: c. 1040-661 BCE'. The page gives the year as the capital's start, not as a founding date.
659: Wey, restored after the Rong killed Duke Yi at Zhaoge in 660 with the help of Duke Huan of Qi, moves its capital to Chuqiu. Infobox 'Chuqiu: 659-629 BCE'; the text dates the attack to 660.

region.text: Xing's seat at Yiyi, 'modern Liaocheng, Shandong'

ledger.note: 635: Wey wipes out the small state of Xing. 'In 635 BCE, during the rule of Marquess Yuan of Xing, the State of Xing was wiped out by the State of Wey.' The Spring and Autumn table gives 632 ('Xing 632 BCE: to Wey'). Xing had been moved to Yiyi (modern Liaocheng) in 662, about 40 km outside Cliopatria's Wey shape; the infobox names Jin and Wey as successors without dividing the land, and the page does not say how long Wey held it, so the keyframes do not draw it.
629: the capital moves to Diqiu, where it stays until 241. Infobox 'Diqiu: 629-241 BCE'; the page gives no reason.

region.text: one cell on the Jin frontier

ledger.note: 550: Cliopatria passes one cell to Jin. Page silent.

450: Cliopatria passes 9 cells (about 1,000 km2) to Jin. Page silent; jin.json records the matching gain, also page-silent. The page says only that Wey had become attached to the House of Zhao of Jin after the Kuaikui-Duke Chu conflict (undated).

region.text: one cell on the Wei frontier

ledger.note: 404: Cliopatria passes one cell to Wei. Page silent.
366: Cliopatria passes 2 cells to Zhao. Page silent.

346: Wey's ruler is downgraded from duke to marquis, and by 320 to 'jun'. 'The ruler was downgraded to marquis in 346 BCE and to jun by 320 BCE.' Same state, same colour; a change of rank, not of land.

region.text: everything of Wey's 350 shape outside the county of Puyang

ledger.note: By 320: Wey is reduced to the county of Puyang. 'by 320 BCE Wey controlled only the county of Puyang.' The page names neither the date of each loss nor who took the land; Wei, which surrounded Wey and later made it a dependency, is the researcher's guess for the counterpart.
241: Qin captures Puyang and Wey's ruler flees to Yewang. Qin captured Puyang 'during its attack on Wei'; Wey survived 'nominally as a Qin vassal with no real independence'.
241: the capital moves from Diqiu to Yewang. Infobox 'Yewang: 241-209 BCE'.

209: Qin Er Shi deposes Lord Jiao and Wey ends, the last of the Zhou fiefs to fall. The traditional account (Shiji) gives 209 BCE and the infobox uses it; a modern revision by Hirase Takao, supported by Zhou Zhenhe, ends his reign in 221 BCE with the Qin conquest of Qi.

wars.name: Rong invasion of Wey
wars.outcome: The Rong attacked Zhaoge and killed Duke Yi; Wey was restored with the help of Duke Huan of Qi and moved to Chuqiu (659).
wars.note: The Spring and Autumn page mentions Duke Huan driving off Northern Di nomads 'after their invasions of Wey and Cai', undated; the Xing page dates the Red Di threat to Xing to 662.

wars.name: Wey's destruction of Xing
wars.outcome: Xing wiped out in 635 (632 in the Spring and Autumn table); Jin and Wey are its listed successors.

wars.name: Qin's capture of Puyang
wars.outcome: Qin captured Puyang during its attack on Wei; Wey's ruler was relocated to Yewang as a nominal Qin vassal.
wars.note: The Wei page opened (Wei surrendered to Qin in 225) says nothing of Puyang.

certainty.note: Wey is a small state on the Yellow River plain whose borders are known only by its capitals and by 'the county of Puyang'; no survey lines exist.

notes: One dossier for Cliopatria's 'Wey' (-750..-248), extended back to c. 1040 and forward to 209 (Shiji; 221 on a modern revision). Cliopatria's shape never changes by more than 9 cells and is about four times the county of Puyang, which is all the page leaves Wey from 320. For the Wei group: the Wey page says Wei made Wey a dependency in 252 and Qin made it a nominal vassal after 241; a vassal_start for each belongs in the Wei and Qin dossiers (there is no way to record 'becomes a vassal' in the vassal's own file). Unsettled: who took Wey's land between the 6th century and 320 (page silent; Cliopatria's small moves to Jin 550/450, Wei 404 and Zhao 366 are not explained); how long Wey held Xing's land (Yiyi) after 635; the Xing date (635 on the Xing page, 632 in the Spring and Autumn table); the 209/221 end. The ruler table on the Wey page was garbled, so no ruler strip is given. Gazetteer: no unknown names; Zhaoge, Chuqiu, Diqiu and Yewang are plain coordinates. The state of Xing needs a dossier or a name only (counterpart 'xing').
